'''Donald Mackay''' {{Post-nominals|country=CAN|OC|OOnt}} (30 October 1936 – 20 October 2023) was a Scottish-born Canadian scientist and engineer specializing in [[environmental chemistry]].

==Life and career==
Donald Mackay was born on 30 October 1936.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.trentu.ca/academic/aminss/envmodel/MackayCV.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae Donald Mackay |date=September 2006 |website=Trent University |accessdate=2013-02-23 |url-status=live |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304053731/http://www.trentu.ca/academic/aminss/envmodel/MackayCV.pdf |archivedate=2016-03-04 }}</ref> He was a member of the faculty of Chemical Engineering and Applied Chemistry at the [[University of Toronto]] and the founding director of the [[Canadian Environmental Modelling Centre]] at [[Trent University]]. He has developed several [[multimedia fugacity model]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mackay|first=Don|date=2021-08-26|title=Fugacity and Multi-Media Models: A Personal Odyssey|url=https://globe.setac.org/fugacity-and-multi-media-models/|url-status=dead |access-date=2021-08-26|website=SETAC Globe|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210826205329/https://globe.setac.org/fugacity-and-multi-media-models/ |archive-date=2021-08-26 }}</ref> He has stressed that principles of [[good practice]] also need to be adopted for chemical assessments, especially in a regulatory context.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Buser |first1=Andreas M |last2=MacLeod |first2=Matthew |last3=Scheringer |first3=Martin |last4=Mackay |first4=Don |last5=Bonnell |first5=Mark |last6=Russell |first6=Mark H |last7=DePinto |first7=Joseph V |last8=Hungerbühler |first8=Konrad |date=8 February 2012 |title=Good modeling practice guidelines for applying multimedia models in chemical assessments |journal=Integrated Environmental Assessment and Management |language=en |volume=8 |issue=4 |pages=703–708 |doi=10.1002/ieam.1299 |pmid=22318971 |bibcode=2012IEAM....8..703B }}</ref>

In 2004, Mackay was invested as an Officer of the [[Order of Canada]] for having "greatly contributed to the quality and our stewardship of the global environment".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-04-30 |title=Donald Mackay, O.C., Ph.D., P. Eng. |url=http://archive.gg.ca/honours/search-recherche/honours-desc.asp?lang=e&TypeID=orc&id=9390 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304081157/http://archive.gg.ca/honours/search-recherche/honours-desc.asp?lang=e&TypeID=orc&id=9390 |archive-date=Mar 4, 2016 |website=Governor General of Canada Archive}}</ref> In 2004, he was also invested into the [[Order of Ontario]] for "his outstanding contributions to environmental science".<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 30, 2005 |title=The Order of Ontario - 2003 Recipients |url=http://www.citizenship.gov.on.ca/english/citdiv/honours/order/order-winners03.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070313002216/http://www.citizenship.gov.on.ca/english/citdiv/honours/order/order-winners03.htm |archive-date=2007-03-13 |website=Ministry of Citizenship and Immigration: The Order of Ontario - 2003 Recipients}}</ref>

Mackay died at the [[Peterborough Regional Health Centre]] on 20 October 2023, at the age of 86.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.legacy.com/ca/obituaries/theglobeandmail/name/donald-mackay-obituary?id=53449377 |date=2023 |title=Donald and Agnes Mackay |work=[[The Globe & Mail]] |via=Legacy.com |access-date=September 14, 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231028093911/https://www.legacy.com/ca/obituaries/theglobeandmail/name/donald-mackay-obituary?id=53449377 |archive-date= 2023-10-28}}</ref>
